role: Command-line front end of the code map: check (the CI gate, failing on unread re-check lines, records naming missing callees or citing line numbers and, when the local findings overlay exists, the open-findings ratchet), status (optionally grouped by callee), sync (with test records prefilled from their code), stamp (any number of records in one pass), ack (clear one callee's re-check lines after re-reading), move (carry records across a file move or unit rename), impact, callers and report. Run by scripts/check_codemap.sh, the codemap-* Makefile targets and the gates.yml impact step.
state: ROOT: repository root (two levels above this file)
OVERLAY: the local, untracked findings overlay, $CODEMAP_OVERLAY or do_not_ship/codemap under ROOT
FLAGS: OVERLAY/flags, one <path>.json per record holding {"file": [...], "units": {key: [...]}}
toplevel: Module docstring (the usage text main prints, including where the findings overlay lives), imports (collections, hashlib, json, os, re, subprocess, sys, Path), ROOT, RECORDS, OVERLAY and FLAGS, sys.path insertion of scripts/codemap so inventory, graph and report import, LINE_CITATION (a `file:line` citation: a known source, project or config file extension, or Makefile, followed by `:` and a number; "line N" prose and a bare `:N` are not matched, being as often data, times or slices) and RECORD_TEXT_FIELDS (the record fields searched for one), and the test-record prefill constants: TEST_ROOTS (EmuquTests/, EmuquUITests/), XCTEST_ENTRY (the XCTest runner trigger of a test method) and XCTEST_HOOKS (setUp/setUpWithError and tearDown/tearDownWithError to their per-test runner triggers). `if __name__ == "__main__": sys.exit(main(argv))`.

units.does: Path of the record for a source path: RECORDS/<path>.json.

Attaches the overlay's findings to a parsed record: when FLAGS/<file>.json exists, sets the record's `flags` to its `file` list and each unit's `flags` to its entry under `units` (empty list when none). With no overlay file the record is returned unchanged, without `flags`. Returns the same dict.

branches.cond: overlay file for this record exists
branches.effect: file and unit flags attached; otherwise record unchanged

units.does: Reads and parses the record for a path and merges the overlay's findings into it (merge_flags); None when the record file does not exist.

Writes a record without findings: works on a deep copy, strips the file-level and unit `flags`, and writes the rest as indented UTF-8 JSON with a trailing newline to docs/codemap/records/<path>.json, creating directories as needed. Findings go only to the overlay: when any are present they are written to FLAGS/<path>.json as {"file": [...], "units": {key: [...]}} (creating the overlay directories); when none are present an existing overlay file for the record is deleted.

branches.cond: no findings and an overlay file exists

units.does: Walks RECORDS with os.walk (so hidden directories such as .github are included) and returns {source path: record} for every .json file, keyed by the record's own `file` field, with the overlay's findings merged into each (merge_flags).

The `file:line` citations (LINE_CITATION matches) in a file record's or unit record's text fields (RECORD_TEXT_FIELDS: role, types, state, toplevel, does, contract, entry, calls, reads, writes, branches), serialized together.

Compares the inventory with the records and returns (path, key, message) for: a file with no record; a stale file hash; an empty role; a file or unit record citing a line number (line_citations); a unit with no record; a unit record with empty `does`; a stale unit hash; a call to a `path::key` that is not a current unit (ext:/dyn:/closure: entries are not checked); a record for a unit no longer in the file; a record file for a path no longer in scope.

branches.effect: one problem; its units are not checked

branches.cond: file record cites a line number

branches.effect: problem; nothing else checked for it

branches.cond: unit record cites a line number
call names a repo unit that is not in the current inventory
record keys with no matching unit
record files for paths not in scope

units.does: Hash (16 hex) of what a record says a unit does, the part callers rely on: for a file record (file_level) its role, toplevel and state; for a unit with a non-blank `contract`, the marker 'contract', the stripped contract, entry, reads and writes; for any other unit its does, entry, reads, writes, and each branch's condition and effect (the same fields, so the hash is unchanged for every record without a contract). Calls, hashes, evidence and findings (flags) are left out, so changing only how a unit is implemented, a branch's line offset, or the local findings overlay does not alter it; for a unit with a contract, neither does rewording does or the branches. None gives ''.

branches.effect: contract, entry, reads, writes; otherwise the whole unit description

units.does: described() for every file record (node `path::`) and every unit record (`path::key`).
The record for a node: the file record for `path::`, otherwise the unit record with that key; None when either is missing.

branches.cond: file has no record, or the node is a file node

units.does: For a node, {callee: described hash} over its certain graph edges, sorted; a callee without a record maps to ''. This is what stamp stores as `deps` and what the re-check compares against.

branches.effect: included; possible edges are left out

units.does: For every file record and unit record whose code hash is current, compares its stored `deps` with current_deps and yields (caller file, caller key, callee node, 'new') for a certain callee missing from deps, or (…, 'changed') for a callee whose described hash differs. Stale records are skipped (the stale line already sends them back). Records with deps entries for callees no longer called are not reported.

Formats recheck_items as problem lines: a 'new' callee gives 're-check: now resolves a call to X, which it was not checked against'; a 'changed' one gives 're-check: X changed what it does since this record was checked'.

branches.effect: the now-resolves line; else the changed line

units.does: Counts findings by severity (high/med/low) across every file-level and unit-level flag in all records. Flags with any other severity are not counted.

branches.cond: severity is high, med or low

units.does: Returns no problems when the findings overlay directory (OVERLAY) does not exist. Otherwise, for high and med: reads OVERLAY/codemap_open_<sev>.txt as an integer and reports a problem (path given relative to the repository root, key "open-findings ratchet") when the open count exceeds it (a change added findings) or is below it (a fix landed without lowering the budget). A missing or non-integer budget file inside an existing overlay is itself a problem, so the ratchet fails closed there.

branches.cond: budget file unreadable or not an integer
more open findings than the budget
fewer open findings than the budget
branches.effect: problem: lower the budget to the new count

units.does: Loads all records (with the overlay's findings when present), builds the inventory and the call graph once. Failing problems: everything problems() reports (records naming missing callees and line citations included), every dependency_problems() re-check line, and the open-findings ratchet (budget_problems over open_findings, which runs only when the overlay exists). With by_callee and re-check lines, first prints them grouped by callee (_print_by_callee over recheck_items, against `base`). No problems: prints success, and when the overlay exists also the open high/medium/low counts, and returns 0. Otherwise prints the problems grouped by file (re-check lines left out when already printed by callee) with how to fix each kind, and returns 1 for `check` (strict) or 0 for `status`.
One line for a record: 'contract: <contract>' when it has one, else its does (or a file record's role); '(no record)' for None.

The record of a node as committed at a git ref: `git show <base>:docs/codemap/records/<file>.json`, then the unit with the node's key (the file record for an empty key); None when the file or unit is not there.

Prints the re-check items grouped by callee, the callee with most callers first: the callee node and its caller count, what its record says now (_what_it_says), what it said at `base` when that differs (_record_at), and each caller, marked when it was not checked against the callee before.
Prints (path, key, message) items grouped by path: the path, then each key (or '(file record)') with its message, indented.
The `///` comment directly above a 1-based line, skipping attribute lines (`@…`), joined into one line without the slashes; '' when there is none.

A test method name as a sentence: drops the 'test' prefix, splits the CamelCase words (acronyms kept together) and lowercases each word except acronyms of two or more capitals: testACancelledDFAWindowIsDropped -> 'a cancelled DFA window is dropped'.

The record sync writes for a new unit: empty except in a Swift file under EmuquTests/ or EmuquUITests/, where a test method (a function named test + capital) gets entry XCTEST_ENTRY and does from its /// comment or, without one, 'Checks that <name as a sentence>.'; setUp/setUpWithError/tearDown/tearDownWithError get their XCTEST_HOOKS entry and their /// comment; any other unit its /// comment. hash stays null, so the record fails check until it is read and stamped.

branches.cond: not a Swift file in a test target

branches.effect: XCTest entry; doc comment or name sentence

units.does: For each given path: if it is not in scope or untracked, deletes its record and its overlay findings file if a record exists (or says to git add it); otherwise loads (with findings) or creates the file record, keeps unit records whose key still exists in code order, adds a prefilled record (hash null) for each new unit from the file's lines, reporting whether it was prefilled or empty, drops records for units no longer in the code, and saves (findings to the overlay only). Never stamps a hash, so new records fail check until read and stamped.
reads: file:<path> (the source, for prefilled test records)

branches.cond: path not tracked or out of scope
branches.effect: removes an existing record, or prints a hint
kept as is; else a prefilled record is added

branches.cond: record for a unit no longer present

units.does: Parses stamp's arguments: when any contains '::', all must be PATH::KEY nodes (PATH:: for a file record), grouped by path in order; else PATH [KEY...], with no KEY meaning the file record (''). None when the two forms are mixed.

branches.effect: grouped nodes, None if any argument is not a node; else the path form

units.does: Marks records as written against the current code, for any number of files in one pass. Builds the full inventory and loads every record once, then checks every target before writing any: refuses (2) when a path is out of scope or has no record, (1) when a file record to stamp has no role, (2) on an unknown key, (1) on a unit with an empty `does`. Then builds the call graph and the descriptions once and, for each target, stores the current code hash (file or unit) and, as `deps`, current_deps of its node; saves each record. It reads nothing for correctness; it trusts that the record was rewritten.

branches.cond: out of scope or no record

branches.effect: file hash and deps; else the unit's

units.does: `ack` for many pairs in one pass: reads `path`, one CALLER<TAB>CALLEE per non-blank line (2 on a line without a tab); builds the inventory, records and graph once; refuses (2, listing up to 20) when any pair is not an open re-check line, writing nothing; otherwise sets each caller's deps[callee] to the callee's current described hash, saves the touched records and prints the count.

branches.cond: a pair is not an open re-check line

units.does: Clears re-check lines for one callee after its callers were re-read and found unaffected: finds the open recheck_items whose callee is `callee`; refuses (1) when there are none and (2) when a named caller has none; for each named caller (every open one when none is named) sets deps[callee] to the callee's current described hash, leaving every other dep, and so every other open line, as it was; saves the touched records and prints each acknowledged caller.

branches.cond: no open line for the callee
a named caller has no open line for it

units.does: Before sync, carries records across a file move or unit rename: parses OLDKEY=NEWKEY pairs (2 on a malformed one); refuses (2) when OLD has no record or NEW already has one; renames the paired unit keys, sets the record's file to NEW and saves it (findings to the overlay at NEW), removing the OLD record and overlay file; then rewrites every record's calls (exact old nodes, then any remaining OLD:: prefix, also inside dyn:/closure: text) and deps keys through moved(), saving only the records that changed. Descriptions and hashes are untouched, so no caller is sent back.
writes: file:docs/codemap/records/** (the moved record and every record naming it)

branches.effect: OLD record and overlay file removed

branches.cond: record named the moved file or units

units.does: One reference rewritten: each OLD::OLDKEY node (longest first) to NEW::NEWKEY, then, when the path changed, any OLD:: not preceded by a path character to NEW::.

Lists (node, 'new'|'changed'|'deleted') for every mapped unit or file-level code whose content differs from `base`. Takes the paths `git diff --name-only <base>` reports (working tree against base), and for each reads the record as it was at base (`git show base:docs/codemap/records/<path>.json`); since the gate passed at base, that record's hashes are base's code hashes. A path out of scope now: if it had a record at base, its file node and units are 'deleted'. Otherwise the file node is 'new' or 'changed' when its hash differs, and each unit is 'new', 'changed' or 'deleted' by key and hash. Exits with a message when the diff fails (unknown ref).

branches.effect: parsed; otherwise treated as empty (everything new)

branches.cond: path not in scope now (deleted, untracked or excluded)
branches.effect: reported only if base had a record
file node and its units reported deleted
file node new (no base hash) or changed

units.does: Prints, as Markdown, what a change can affect. Targets: the named `path::key` nodes, or changed_since(base) (base from `--base REF`, default origin/main). An unknown named node prints up to 15 nodes containing its short name and returns 2. For each target: what its record says it does; direct callers, certain listed in full and possible up to 40; a walk up certain callers that stops at tests and doc sections (collected) and collects every caller with an `entry` as a trigger (up to 80 listed); for unit targets, each store it reads or writes (prefix up to ' (') with how many other units read and write it and up to 12 of them; and the open flags on the target and its certain direct callers (present only when the local findings overlay is merged in). The same text is appended to $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY (up to 900,000 characters) when that is set. Returns 0.

branches.effect: base taken from the next argument

branches.cond: a named node is not in the graph
target has a record and still exists

branches.effect: collected as a test, not walked further
collected as a doc, not walked further
listed as a trigger; walk continues past it
text appended to the job summary

units.does: Prints each direct caller of one node with its edge kind (certain first, then possible, each sorted), or a hint about the key format when there are none. Returns 0.

Dispatches argv: no args or -h/--help prints the usage and returns 0; check -> strict check; status -> non-strict, or grouped by callee with `--by-callee [BASE]`; sync PATH...; stamp with stamp_targets' groups (2 when the forms are mixed); ack --from FILE -> cmd_ack_from; ack CALLEE [CALLER...]; move OLD NEW [OLDKEY=NEWKEY...]; impact [--base REF] [NODE...]; callers NODE; report OUTDIR -> report.build over all records. Anything else prints the usage to stderr and returns 2.
units.entry: python3 scripts/codemap/codemap.py <command> (check_codemap.sh, the codemap-* Makefile targets, the gates.yml impact step, by hand)

branches.effect: by callee with --by-callee, else non-strict check
cmd_stamp, or 2 when the forms are mixed
